scope: Same code, same inputs, different machine: the Mac release build against the container reference build of the same run id. Not used for the release-vs-c066 comparison.
principle: Every GOLD file must be identical after run-id normalisation. The only exceptions are the outputs listed here, each limited to named fields or bounded counts. Every allowed difference is reported; anything else fails the gate.

rules.why: A family name is a descriptive label: the top TF-IDF terms of its member courses. Exact ties are broken by term since 2026-10-09; a near-tie whose last bit differs between libm/BLAS builds can still swap two terms. Membership, uids and evidence must be identical.
Carries the family name above. Every other field, including candidate_related_concepts (deterministically ordered since 2026-10-09), must be identical.
The HIGH-priority subset of the review queue; same reason.
A segment label is the top TF-IDF terms of its postings (descriptive). Segment membership, sizes and demand must be identical.

Peer comparison ranks cosine similarities between thousands of topic pairs and keeps those above a threshold. Similarities within a few ulps of the threshold or of each other resolve differently on OpenBLAS and Apple Accelerate. Only review-required AMBIGUOUS and context-only RELATED relations may move, within the count tolerance per peer curriculum, and at most a quarter of their records may differ (records differing / reference count; observed 2026-10-09: at most 16%). SAME_CONCEPT, PARTIAL_OVERLAP and every other relation must be identical record for record.
The review-required subset of peer_relations; same reason.

Summaries of the peer relations above: review-required and related counts, their percentages, the capped example lists, and the peer curriculum's concept count (peer concepts are clustered on the same similarities). Supported SAME_CONCEPT coverage, ABSENT_IN_COMPARISON, lexical coverage, depth, skill rows and industry alignment must be identical.
